--- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.add_random_partition_graph()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: >- Add a random partition graph: groups of given sizes with random edges. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.add_random_partition_graph()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: >- Add a random partition graph: groups of given sizes with random edges. title: >- [Graph.add_random_partition_graph()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: >- Add a random partition graph: groups of given sizes with random edges. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Add a random partition graph: groups of given sizes with random edges. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L13362-L13480){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.add_random_partition_graph( sizes, p_in, p_out, seed=None, community_attr="community", type=None, label=True, rel=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Random partition graph](/assets/graphs/add-random-partition-graph.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Three random partition graphs with groups of the sizes given, each group in its own color: two groups of four, groups of two, three, and four, and groups of two, two, three, and four. Edges appear with probability 0.9 inside a group and 0.1 between groups, so each group is dense and the few plain edges link them." width="100%"} Creates one group of nodes per entry of `sizes=` and joins each pair of nodes at random: with probability `p_in` if they are in the same group and with probability `p_out` if they are not, every pair independently. It generalizes the planted partition graph (see `add_planted_partition_graph()`) to groups of different sizes, and is the stochastic block model with only two probabilities; for a full matrix of block probabilities see `generate_stochastic_block_model()`. Each node's group (`0`, `1`, ...) is stored in the `community_attr=` node attribute, so the planted communities can be compared with what a detection method finds. The groups are created in order, each as a consecutive run of node IDs. In an undirected graph each pair is joined at most once and edges point from the earlier-created node to the later one; in a directed graph each ordered pair is drawn separately, so two nodes may be joined in both directions. The graph is appended without touching or connecting to existing nodes, and the whole construction is recorded as a single step. Random partition graphs are useful for: - benchmarking community detection on groups of unequal sizes, which many methods find harder than equal groups - modeling populations with groups of known sizes (departments, classes, regions) and a uniform tendency to connect within them - null models that keep a known group structure but randomize everything else ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [sizes]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Number of nodes in each group, e.g. `[10, 20, 40]`. Every size must be non-negative. [p_in]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Probability of an edge between two nodes in the same group, between `0` and `1`. [p_out]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Probability of an edge between two nodes in different groups, between `0` and `1`. [seed]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Integer seed for the random number generator. The same `seed=` with the same other arguments always gives the same graph. If `None` (default), the graph differs on every call. [community_attr]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["community"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Name of the node attribute that records each node's group. Default is `"community"`. Pass `None` to skip storing it. [type]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `type` attribute of every new node. If `None` (default), no `type` attribute is set. [label]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True` (default), each new node is labelled with its node ID as a string; a label that is already used raises `ValueError` before anything is added. If `False`, the nodes are left unlabelled. [rel]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `rel` attribute of every new edge. If `None` (default), no `rel` attribute is set. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Self for method chaining. The graph is modified in place. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If an entry of `sizes=` is negative, or `p_in=` or `p_out=` is not between `0` and `1`. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Three groups of `10`, `20`, and `40` nodes: ::: {#a5599aef .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph().add_random_partition_graph( sizes=[10, 20, 40], p_in=0.4, p_out=0.02, seed=3 ) graph.get_node_df()["community"].value_counts().sort("community") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ```{=html}
